title: The red crayon
basis: Desire-based emotion (Pons, Harris & de Rosnay, Test of Emotion Comprehension): the same event makes one child happy and another sad because they wanted different things; understood from about age 5.
text: You and Meera both want the red crayon. You get it first. Meera looks sad. She wanted to colour a red apple. What do you do?
hint: What did Meera want to colour?
options: Use it quickly, then give it to Meera
Meera waits. Soon her apple is red too.
Keep it. I got it first
You colour happily. Meera sits quietly with no red.
Hide the crayon in my bag
Meera looks everywhere. Now nobody is colouring.

title: The wet drawing
basis: Ambiguous provocation and hostile attribution (Dodge, social information processing): checking before assuming someone meant harm.
text: Kabir walks past your desk. Your water bottle falls and wets your drawing. Kabir stops and looks at the puddle. Did he mean it? What do you do?
hint: Do you know yet if Kabir did it on purpose?
options: Ask, "Was that an accident?"
"Sorry! My bag hit it," Kabir says. He helps you wipe it.
Shout at Kabir and push him
Kabir looks shocked. The teacher comes, and you both feel bad.
Wipe it and stay quiet all day
The drawing dries a little, but you feel upset all day.

title: Hot face at the swings
basis: Gross process model of emotion regulation: noticing the body's signals of anger before acting on them.
text: You were waiting for the swing. Riya runs and takes it first. Your face feels hot. Your hands make fists. What do you do?
hint: What is your body telling you?
options: Take three big, slow breaths
Your hands relax. Now you can think about what to say.
Pull Riya off the swing
Riya slips onto the sand and starts to cry.
Run off and hide
The angry feeling stays, and you miss your turn.

title: Ice cream after dinner
basis: Inhibitory control and delay of gratification (Diamond 2013): waiting for something tempting, helped by a smart way to wait.
text: Papa bought ice cream. He says, "We will eat it after dinner." The freezer is right there. Papa is busy on the phone. What do you do?
hint: What could you do so you don't think about it?
options: Go and draw until dinner
Dinner comes fast. Then everyone has ice cream together.
Eat a big spoon now, quietly
It is yummy, but Papa finds the open box later.
Ask Papa, "Can I have some now?"
Papa says, "After dinner," and you wait a long time.

title: The broken cup
basis: WHO life skills (decision making): owning up to a mistake nobody saw, and helping put it right.
text: You are playing ball inside. The ball hits Mummy's cup and it breaks. Nobody saw. Mummy calls, "What was that noise?" What do you do?
hint: How would you want someone to tell you?
options: Say, "It was me. I'm sorry."
Mummy looks sad about her cup, but thanks you for telling her.
Say, "The cat did it!"
Mummy looks at the sleepy cat. Your tummy feels heavy.
Hide the pieces under the sofa
Later Mummy finds them and is upset nobody told her.

title: Alone at lunch
basis: Inclusion of a child who is different (WHO life skills: empathy); upstander responses at an age-appropriate level.
text: Tenzin is new. He speaks only a little Hindi. He sits alone at lunch. Your friends say, "Don't sit with him." What do you do?
hint: How might Tenzin feel, sitting alone?
options: Tell my friends, "Tenzin can sit with us!"
One friend frowns, but Tenzin smiles and sits with you.
Do what my friends say
Tenzin eats alone again. He looks at the floor.
Tell the teacher Tenzin is alone
The teacher helps Tenzin find a place to sit.

title: Lost at the market
basis: WHO life skills (coping with stress): help-seeking through a trusted grown-up; staying put when lost.
text: You are at the market with Papa. You stop to look at balloons. Now you cannot see Papa! Your heart beats fast. What do you do?
options: Stay here and ask the shopkeeper
The shopkeeper calls out loudly. Papa hurries back and holds your hand.
Run around looking for Papa
Everything looks different, and it is harder to find Papa.
Walk home by myself
The road is long. Papa is still searching at the market.

title: One tablet, two children
basis: Fairness and turn-taking in early and middle childhood: finding a fair way that works for both.
text: There is one tablet. You and your little sister Diya both want to play now. What do you do?
hint: Is there a way you can both have a go?
options: Set a timer and take turns
Ding! Your turn ends, Diya plays, and nobody fights.
Grab it and play first
Diya cries, and Mummy puts the tablet away.
Give it to her and sulk
Diya is happy, but you feel left out all evening.

title: Quiet in the library
basis: Turiel social domain theory: young children can see that someone being hurt matters more than a 'be quiet' rule.
text: In the library, everyone must be quiet. Your friend Anjali trips and hurts her knee. She is crying. What do you do?
options: Stay quiet. That is the rule
Anjali keeps crying, and nobody comes to help her.
Go and tell the teacher quickly
The teacher comes fast and puts a plaster on Anjali's knee.
Laugh because she fell
Anjali feels worse, and she turns away from you.

title: "I don't care"
basis: Hidden emotion (Pons, Harris & de Rosnay, Test of Emotion Comprehension): noticing a clue that someone feels different inside from what they show.
text: Ishaan is not picked for the race. He says, "I don't care." But his eyes look wet, and he looks at the ground. What do you do?
hint: What do Ishaan's eyes tell you?
options: Sit with him and ask, "Are you sad?"
Ishaan nods a little. You sit together and watch the race.
Say, "Okay!" and run to the race
You run off. Ishaan sits alone on the steps.
Say, "Don't cry. It's only a race."
Ishaan turns away and wipes his eyes.

title: A message in the game
basis: Online safety: never sharing personal details with someone unknown, and telling a trusted grown-up.
text: You are playing a game on Mummy's phone. A message pops up: "Hi! What is your name and school?" You don't know who it is. What do you do?
hint: Who should know about this message?
options: Show Mummy the message
Mummy reads it and blocks it. You keep playing safely.
Type my name and school
Mummy sees it later and turns the chat off.
Close the game and say nothing
The message is gone, but you keep thinking about it.

title: My tower, my turn
basis: WHO life skills (effective communication): saying clearly and calmly what you need, instead of hitting out or staying silent.
text: You are building a tower with blocks. Bunty keeps taking your blocks for his car. You feel cross. What do you do?
hint: How could you keep your tower and still play nicely?
options: Say, "Please stop. I need those blocks."
Bunty frowns, then puts some blocks back.
Knock his car over
Bunty shouts, and now both games are broken.
Let him take them all
Your tower gets smaller and smaller. You feel sad inside.

title: Ro's balloons
basis: Early number: adding within 10 with a story.
text: Ro has 3 balloons. Kiki gives him 2 more. How many balloons does Ro have now?
options: Count again. One balloon is hiding!
Ro holds all his balloons up high!
That is one balloon more than Ro has.

title: Mangoes in the basket
basis: Early number: taking away within 10 with a story.
text: There are 7 mangoes in a basket. Meera eats 2. How many mangoes are left?
options: Count back again, slowly from 7.
Five mangoes wait in the basket.
Eating makes fewer mangoes, not more.

title: Kiki's bead necklace
basis: Early reasoning: continuing a repeating pattern.
text: Kiki makes a necklace: red bead, blue bead, red bead, blue bead, red bead. Which colour comes next?
hint: Say the colours out loud. What do you hear?
options: Red
Two reds side by side break the pattern.
Blue
Red, blue, red, blue. Kiki's necklace is perfect!
Green
There is no green bead in this pattern yet.

puzzle.explanation: The colours take turns: red, blue, red, blue. After red comes blue.

title: Big and small
text: The elephant is big. The mouse is the opposite of big. What is the mouse?
hint: Think of the tiniest animal you know.
options: Small
The tiny mouse squeaks and runs away!
Grey
Grey is a colour. The mouse can be grey and small.
Loud
Loud is about sound. The mouse is very quiet.

puzzle.explanation: Big and small are opposites. The elephant is big, so the mouse is small.
